state.name: Uttar Pradesh
state.description: Uttar Pradesh is culturally and historically significant.
state.culturalSummary: Hindu traditions, festivals, and classical arts define culture.

artAndHandicrafts.name: Chikankari
artAndHandicrafts.description: A traditional embroidery style from Lucknow.

artAndHandicrafts.name: Brassware
artAndHandicrafts.description: Moradabad is known as the 'Brass City' for its famous brass handicrafts.

cuisine.description: Awadhi and Mughlai cuisines are the jewels of UP. The state offers a royal feast of kebabs, biryanis, and rich vegetarian dishes.

dishes.name: Galouti Kebab
dishes.description: Melt-in-the-mouth minced meat kebabs, originally made for a toothless Nawab.

dishes.name: Peda
dishes.description: A famous sweet from Mathura made of khoya and cardamom.

dishes.name: Tehri
dishes.description: A yellow rice dish cooked with potatoes and vegetables, a staple in every household.

culturalPlaces.name: Taj Mahal
culturalPlaces.description: An immense mausoleum of white marble, built in Agra between 1631 and 1648.

culturalPlaces.name: Varanasi Ghats
culturalPlaces.description: Riverfront steps leading to the banks of the River Ganges.

culturalPlaces.name: Bara Imambara
culturalPlaces.description: A large complex built by Asaf-ud-Daula, Nawab of Awadh, in 1784.

dances.name: Kathak
dances.description: One of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance, originating from the bards of ancient northern India.

dances.name: Charkula
dances.description: A dance performed in the Braj region where women balance oil lamps on their heads.

music.name: Thumri
music.description: A semi-classical music form that originated in UP, often revolving around the love of Radha and Krishna.

instruments.name: Tabla
instruments.description: A membranophone percussion instrument associated with Kathak and Hindustani classical music.

instruments.name: Shehnai
instruments.description: Made famous by Ustad Bismillah Khan of Varanasi, played during weddings and auspicious occasions.

extraSections.title: Languages
extraSections.content: Hindi and Urdu are the official and most widely spoken languages using the Devanagari and Perso-Arabic scripts respectively. Awadhi, Braj, and Bhojpuri are popular dialects.

festivals.name: Kumbh Mela
festivals.significance: Largest peaceful gathering in the world.
festivals.description: Millions of devotees gather to bathe in the sacred rivers.

festivals.name: Holi in Braj
festivals.description: Lathmar Holi in Barsana is particularly famous.

festivals.name: Diwali in Ayodhya
festivals.description: The city is lit up with millions of diyas (lamps).

customs.title: Ganga Aarti
customs.description: Performed daily at dusk at the Dashashwamedh Ghat in Varanasi.

rituals.title: Mundan
rituals.description: First haircut ceremony for children, often performed at river banks.

heritageAndTraditions.dailyLife: Many people start their day with visits to temples. In cities, the culture is a mix of modern hustle and traditional values.
heritageAndTraditions.values: Respect for elders and communal harmony (Ganga-Jamuni Tehzeeb) are core values.

overview.introduction: Uttar Pradesh is the rainbow land where the multi-hued Indian Culture has blossomed from times immemorial. Blessed with a variety of geographical land and many cultural biodiversities, UP has been the area of activity of historical heroes like Rama, Krishna, Buddha, Taj Mahal and the British Raj.
overview.lifestyle: The lifestyle is deeply rooted in tradition, with a blend of rural simplicity and urban modernization. Family values are paramount, and hospitality (Mehman-nawazi) is a way of life.
overview.traditions: From the Ganga Aarti in Varanasi to the Tehzeeb (etiquette) of Lucknow, UP is a melting pot of Hindu and Mughal traditions.
overview.history: Uttar Pradesh has been the cradle of Indian civilization, witnessing the rise and fall of empires like the Mauryas, Guptas, and Mughals.

men.description: Traditional dress includes Kurta-Pajama or Dhoti-Kurta, often accompanied by a Gamcha or Topi.

women.description: Sarees are the most common, especially the Banarasi Silk Saree which is world-famous.

attire.name: Banarasi Saree
attire.description: Opulent silk sarees with gold and silver brocade.

fabrics.name: Chikankari
fabrics.description: Delicate and shadow work embroidery from Lucknow.

foodTrails.name: Lucknow Street Food Walk
foodTrails.description: Explore the best Tunday Kababs and Chaat in Aminabad.

cities.name: Lucknow
cities.description: Lucknow is the capital city of Uttar Pradesh and a major cultural, administrative, and educational center known for its Nawabi heritage and refined lifestyle.
cities.history: Lucknow rose to prominence under the Nawabs of Awadh and played a significant role during the 1857 revolt.

cities.name: Varanasi
cities.description: Varanasi is one of the oldest living cities in the world and a major spiritual hub situated on the banks of the Ganga River.
cities.history: Varanasi has been a center of learning and spirituality for over 3000 years and is deeply connected to Hindu philosophy.

cities.name: Agra
cities.description: Agra is a historic city globally famous for the Taj Mahal and a major tourist destination of India.
cities.history: Agra served as the capital of the Mughal Empire under emperors like Akbar and Shah Jahan.

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.description: The Taj Mahal is one of the Seven Wonders of the World and the most iconic monument of India, symbolizing love and Mughal architectural brilliance.

places.name: Agra Fort
places.description: Agra Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site built with red sandstone and served as the main residence of Mughal emperors.

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri
places.description: Fatehpur Sikri is a historic Mughal city near Agra, famous for its well-preserved palaces, mosques, and courtyards.

places.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
places.description: Itmad-ud-Daulah, also known as Baby Taj, is known for its intricate marble inlay work and beautiful gardens.

places.name: Mehtab Bagh
places.description: Mehtab Bagh is a Mughal garden complex located opposite the Taj Mahal and offers stunning sunset views.

places.name: Akbar’s Tomb, Sikandra
places.description: Akbar’s Tomb is the burial place of Mughal Emperor Akbar and reflects a unique blend of architectural styles.

foods.name: Petha
foods.description: Petha is a famous sweet made from ash gourd and sugar syrup, available in many flavors like plain, kesar, and angoori.
foods.famousFor: Signature sweet of Agra, especially popular among tourists

foods.name: Bedai with Aloo Sabzi
foods.description: Bedai is a deep-fried, spicy wheat bread served with tangy potato curry, commonly eaten as breakfast.

foods.name: Mughlai Chicken
foods.description: Mughlai Chicken is a rich and creamy curry prepared with spices, nuts, and slow-cooked chicken.
foods.famousFor: Influence of Mughal cuisine in Agra

foods.name: Dal Moth
foods.description: Dal Moth is a crunchy snack made with fried lentils, nuts, and spices, popular as a tea-time snack.

foods.name: Kachori
foods.description: Kachori is a deep-fried pastry filled with spiced lentils or peas, commonly enjoyed with chutney.
foods.famousFor: Popular North Indian street food in Agra

foods.name: Butter Chicken
foods.description: Butter Chicken is a creamy tomato-based curry with tender chicken pieces, mildly spiced and rich.
foods.famousFor: Popular North Indian non-veg dish enjoyed in Agra

transports.description: State-run and private buses operate regularly from Agra to nearby and distant cities.
transports.connectivity: Connected to Delhi, Jaipur, Lucknow, Kanpur and other major North Indian cities

transports.description: Agra has multiple major railway stations including Agra Cantt and Raja Ki Mandi.
transports.connectivity: Well connected to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and other major cities

transports.description: Agra is served by Kheria Airport with limited domestic flights.
transports.connectivity: Direct flights available to selected cities; major international flights via Delhi

transports.description: Taxis and cab services are widely available for local sightseeing and intercity travel.
transports.connectivity: Available throughout the city and for outstation trips to Delhi and Jaipur

transports.description: Auto-rickshaws are a common and affordable mode of transport within the city.
transports.connectivity: Easily available near markets, stations, and tourist areas

transports.description: Currently, Agra Metro is under development to improve urban connectivity.
transports.connectivity: Planned to connect major residential and tourist areas of the city

cities.name: Prayagraj
cities.description: Prayagraj is a sacred city located at the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers and is known for the Kumbh Mela.
cities.history: Formerly Allahabad, the city has ancient religious and political significance.

cities.name: Ayodhya
cities.description: Ayodhya is a revered religious city believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama and an important pilgrimage destination.
cities.history: Ayodhya is mentioned in ancient Hindu scriptures like the Ramayana and has a long cultural history.

cities.name: Mathura
cities.description: Mathura is a holy city associated with the birth of Lord Krishna and part of the Braj region.
cities.history: Mathura flourished under ancient dynasties such as the Kushans and Guptas.

cities.name: Kanpur
cities.description: Kanpur is one of the largest industrial cities of Uttar Pradesh and a major commercial hub.
cities.history: Kanpur played an important role during the 1857 revolt and later developed as an industrial center.

cities.name: Jhansi
cities.description: Jhansi is a historic city associated with Rani Lakshmibai and India’s freedom struggle.
cities.history: Jhansi Fort symbolizes resistance during the 1857 uprising against British rule.

cities.name: Meerut
cities.description: Meerut is a major city in western Uttar Pradesh and an important commercial and educational center.
cities.history: Meerut is historically significant as the starting point of the 1857 First War of Independence.

cities.name: Gorakhpur
cities.description: Gorakhpur is an important city in eastern Uttar Pradesh known for religious significance and transport connectivity.
cities.history: The city is named after Guru Gorakhnath and has long spiritual importance.

cities.name: Noida
cities.description: Noida is a planned city in western Uttar Pradesh and a major IT, corporate, and residential hub within the National Capital Region.
cities.history: Noida was established in 1976 as part of urban industrial development near Delhi.

cities.name: Ghaziabad
cities.description: Ghaziabad is an important industrial and residential city in western Uttar Pradesh, forming a key part of the NCR.
cities.history: Ghaziabad was founded in 1740 and grew rapidly due to its proximity to Delhi.

cities.name: Bareilly
cities.description: Bareilly is a major city in the Rohilkhand region of Uttar Pradesh known for trade, education, and cultural heritage.
cities.history: Bareilly was founded in 1657 and has historical importance during Mughal and British periods.

cities.name: Aligarh
cities.description: Aligarh is an educational and commercial center of western Uttar Pradesh, globally known for Aligarh Muslim University.
cities.history: Aligarh rose to prominence in the 19th century with the establishment of AMU.

cities.name: Moradabad
cities.description: Moradabad is an industrial city famous for brass handicrafts and export trade.
cities.history: Moradabad was founded in 1600 by Prince Murad and later became a major trading center.

cities.name: Saharanpur
cities.description: Saharanpur is known for wood carving industries and its agricultural economy.
cities.history: Saharanpur developed during Mughal rule and later under British administration.

cities.name: Firozabad
cities.description: Firozabad is known as the glassware city of India and is a major industrial center.
cities.history: Firozabad developed during the Mughal era and expanded during British rule.

cities.name: Muzaffarnagar
cities.description: Muzaffarnagar is an important agricultural and sugarcane-producing city of western Uttar Pradesh.
cities.history: Muzaffarnagar was established in the Mughal period and grew as a trade center.

cities.name: Shahjahanpur
cities.description: Shahjahanpur is a historic city known for its role in the freedom movement and military heritage.
cities.history: The city was founded by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and later gained importance during British rule.

cities.name: Faizabad
cities.description: Faizabad is a historic city closely associated with Ayodhya and Awadh culture.
cities.history: Faizabad served as the capital of Awadh before Lucknow.
